author: Ivan Petrović
title_sr: Javno nadmetanje za zakup i korišćenje poljoprivrednog zemljišta u državnoj svojini isključivo putem veb-aplikacije
body_sr:
Ministarstvo poljoprivrede, šumarstva i vodoprivrede Republike Srbije donelo je izmene Pravilnika o uslovima i postupku davanja u zakup i na korišćenje poljoprivrednog zemljišta u državnoj svojini („Službeni glasnik RS“, br. 16/2017, 111/2017, 18/2019, 45/2019, 3/2020, 25/2020, 133/2020 i 63/2021, u daljem tekstu Pravilnik). Izmene su stupile na snagu 24. juna 2021. godine.

Prethodna verzija Pravilnika predviđala je dva načina sprovođenja javnog nadmetanja za zakup ili korišćenje poljoprivrednog zemljišta u državnoj svojini. Prvi je bio klasično javno nadmetanje, koje je zahtevalo lično prisustvo, a drugi elektronsko javno nadmetanje putem veb-aplikacije Uprave za poljoprivredno zemljište.

Najznačajnija novina ovih izmena jeste potpuno ukidanje javnog nadmetanja uz lično prisustvo. Fizička i pravna lica registrovana kao poljoprivredna gazdinstva, koja imaju pravo da učestvuju u ovim nadmetanjima, od stupanja izmena na snagu mogu da učestvuju isključivo elektronski. [Veb-aplikacija za elektronsko javno nadmetanje](https://gp.upz.minpolj.gov.rs/InzemBid)

Sprovođenje upravnih postupaka elektronskim putem dobrodošao je pravac razvoja koji je u Srbiji prisutan već neko vreme, naročito od donošenja Zakona o elektronskoj upravi 2018. godine („Službeni glasnik RS“, br. 27/2018). Osnovna ideja tog zakona bila je da se licima pruži dodatni način ostvarivanja prava pred organima uprave, uz mogućnost izbora. Zakon nije propisao da se postojeći postupci koji podrazumevaju neposredan kontakt u potpunosti zamene elektronskim postupcima i da se učesnicima ukine mogućnost ličnog prisustva.

Zato se postavlja pitanje kakve će posledice ove izmene imati za zainteresovane učesnike. U javnim nadmetanjima za zakup ili korišćenje poljoprivrednog zemljišta učestvuju poljoprivredna gazdinstva, koja posluju u sektoru manje oslonjenom na elektronsko poslovanje. Ostaje da se vidi da li će prelazak na isključivo elektronsko nadmetanje tim učesnicima olakšati ili otežati učešće.
title_en: Public bidding for lease/use of state-owned agricultural land exclusively via web application
body_en:
The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of the Republic of Serbia introduced newest amendments of the Rulebook on Conditions and Procedure for Public Bidding for Lease/Use of State Owned Agricultural Land (“Official Gazette of RS”, no. 16/2017, 111/2017, 18/2019, 45/2019, 3/2020, 25/2020, 133/2020 and 63/2021) (the “Rulebook”) that came into force on 24 June 2021.

Previous version of Rulebook prescribed two possible manners for conducting the public bidding for lease/use of state owned agricultural land – regular - “old-school” public bidding that requires physical presence, and e-public bidding that is conducted through web application provided by the Administration for Agricultural Land.

The most notable novelty of the latest amendments of the Rulebook is the complete elimination of regular “old-school” public bidding. From now on, natural and legal persons registered as agricultural holdings, being the subjects entitled to participate in respective public biddings, can participate in public biddings only electronically through mentioned web application. The web application for digital public bidding can be accessed by the [following link](https://gp.upz.minpolj.gov.rs/InzemBid).

The trend of conducting administrative procedures through electronic means is welcomed and ongoing in Serbia for a while now, and especially since 2018 when the Law on Electronic Administration (“Official Gazette of RS”, no. 27/2018) was introduced. However, the main idea of this law was to provide for yet another possibility in realization of one’s rights before the administrative bodies, which assumes the choice of a subject at hand. It was never prescribed that existing procedures that assume personal “face-to-face” contact should be completely replaced by e-procedures and subjects deprived from the possibility to take part in these procedures physically - “in person”.

Having this in mind, it stands to question the latest amendments of the Rulebook, especially from the perspective of interested subject – since the participants in public biddings for lease/use of agricultural land are agricultural holdings/subjects and not subjects who come from sectors more focused on digital/electronic environment of doing business – it is left to be seen whether the effects of the latest amendments of the Rulebook are going to be positive or negative for the bidders.
